newsitem.title: GERMANY: Giscard says no problem with mark-french rate.
newsitem.headline: Giscard says no problem with mark-french rate.

text.p: Former French President Valery Giscard d'Estaing said on Thursday he was not seeking a devaluation of the French franc against the mark, but said a stronger dollar would be useful for France's economy.

"The link between the franc and the mark is no problem," he said, adding the problem was the relation between the franc and the dollar. He would prefer to see the dollar at a rate of 5.5 francs per dollar from around 5.0 currently.

Speaking to a group of journalists after talks with German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, Giscard d'Estaing said he had not been advocating a depreciation of the franc against the mark in a French magazine article on Wednesday.
"Currencies (in the EMU) do not have a fixed parity," he said. "They are floating and only obliged to stay within the 15 percent band."

Giscard d'Estaing had called in a magazine article for a sharp depreciation in the franc against the dollar, implying a similar big fall against the mark, to revive growth and employment. His comments have slightly weakened the franc against the mark.

"The dollar at 5.5 French francs would be better and would enable the French economy to go back to growth and employment," he said in Bonn after a 75-minute meeting with Kohl that he described as "warm and friendly."
